chunks: About a woman who dies during travel while no mahram and no women are with her, he said: “She should be buried as she is, in her clothes.”
And [about] a man who dies while only women are with him and there are no men with them, he said: “They should bury him as he is, in his clothes.”

key_terms.الرَّجُلُ: the man whose burial ruling is also asked about
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel; the circumstance in which the death occurs
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman whose burial situation is being asked about
key_terms.بِثِيَابِهَا: in her clothes, without removing them
key_terms.ذُو مَحْرَمٍ: a male relative within the prohibited degrees of marriage

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman or man dies while traveling and only unrelated members of the opposite sex are present?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for burial when a deceased person is among members of the opposite sex without anyone permitted to handle the body in the usual way. In such a case, the deceased is buried as they are, in their clothes, preserving modesty and observing legal limits.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.428 - Al-Halabi asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)

about a woman who dies while traveling, with no male relative (mahram) or other women present.
Imam (as) replied: "She should be buried as She is, in her clothes”.

He (Halabi) asked; Regarding a man who dies with only women present and no other men.
Imam said: "They should bury him as he is, in his clothes."
